newsitem.title: UK: Princess Diana plans to sell 65 evening dresses.
newsitem.headline: Princess Diana plans to sell 65 evening dresses.

text.p: Princess Diana is planning to donate her wedding dress to a British museum and to sell 65 evening dresses for charity, a newspaper said on Wednesday.
The Daily Telegraph said the ex-wife of heir-to-the-throne Prince Charles is determined to redefine her image and "pursue a new role outside the conventional royal mould."
"Next month, she will announce that she intends to give the dress which stunned the world in 1981 to the Victoria & Albert Museum for permanent public display," the newspaper said.
"At the same time, she will announce the most glamourous second-hand clothes sale in history with a proposed auction of 65 evening dresses in June."
The charity sale, expected to be held at Christie's auction house, could make more than one million pounds ($1.61 million) for her favourite charities.

Diana, one of the most photographed women in the world, is renowned for her fashion sense and designer wardrobe. Fashion experts say the auction could generate the same kind of interest as last year's auction of the belongings of Jaqueline Onassis.
The Telegraph said Diana's decision to sell her old clothes illustrates her determination to portray herself as an independent woman.
Her recent trip to Angola on behalf of the Red Cross to publicise the dangers of landmines set a new casual, informal style which the princess is interested in continuing.
